heroHeadline: British Columbia Ends Wildfire State of Emergency as Bald Range Fire Holds at 25,185 Hectares
heroSubtitle: British Columbia lifted its province-wide wildfire state of emergency on August 27 — two days ahead of the scheduled extension — after officials determined its emergency powers were no longer needed, though roughly 206 wildfires continue burning and local evacuation orders remain in force. The Bald Range fire near Summerland held steady at 25,185 hectares as of August 28 after the season's first significant rain reached the fireline, prompting further evacuation-order rescissions near Agur Lake and on Bathville Road. In Northwestern Ontario, evacuees from Eabametoong, Gull Bay and Lac Des Mille Lacs First Nations have all returned home even as three small new fires nudged the region's active count to 59; the Thunder Bay 36 fire and the rest of the Rinker Lake Complex remain not under control despite low activity. Nationally, 582 wildfires remain active (31 out of control) across 4,793 fires and 4.1 million hectares burned this season, per the federal government's most recent (Aug 18) figures. Five deaths remain confirmed this season.
